chunks: A number of our companions, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan ibn Yazid, from Badr, from his father, who said: Sallam Abu Ali Al-Khurasani narrated to me, from Sallam ibn Sa'id Al-Makhzumi, who said:

While I was sitting in the presence of Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), there entered upon him 'Abbad ibn Kathir, the devotee of the people of Al-Basra, and Ibn Shurayh, the jurist of the people of Makkah; and with Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) was Maymun Al-Qaddah, the mawla of Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام).

'Abbad ibn Kathir asked him and said: 'O Abu 'Abdillah, in how many garments was Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) shrouded?' He said: 'In three garments: two Suhari garments and one Hibarah garment, and there was scarcity regarding al-burd.' It was as though 'Abbad ibn Kathir turned away in disapproval at that, so Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) said: 'Indeed, the palm tree of Maryam (عليها السلام) was only 'ajwah, and it descended from the heaven. So whatever grew from its root was 'ajwah, and whatever was from scattered pickings, then it is a mixed color.'

So when they left his presence, 'Abbad ibn Kathir said to Ibn Shurayh: 'By Allah, I do not know what this parable was that Abu 'Abdillah gave me.' Ibn Shurayh said: 'This young man will inform you, for he is from them'—meaning Maymun. So he asked him, and Maymun said: 'Do you not know what he said to you?' He said: 'No, by Allah.' He said: 'He gave you a parable of himself, informing you that he is a descendant from the descendants of Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and the knowledge of Rasul Allah is with them. So whatever comes from them is correct, and whatever comes from other than them is mere gleanings.'

key_terms.حِبَرَةٍ: a patterned Yemeni garment used as a shroud cloth here
key_terms.عَجْوَةً: a prized kind of date, used here to indicate pure original stock
key_terms.عِلْمُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the knowledge of Rasul Allah, described as being with the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.لُقَاطٍ: gleanings or mixed offshoot produce, used metaphorically for what is taken from outside the true source
key_terms.نَخْلَةَ مَرْيَمَ: the palm tree associated with Maryam (عليها السلام), used here as a parable

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in transmitting the knowledge of Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a question posed to Imam Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) about the shrouding of Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), followed by a symbolic answer clarifying the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in preserving the Prophet’s knowledge. Its significance lies in affirming that true knowledge is inherited through them, and that what comes from other sources lacks the same certainty.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan Bin Yazeed, from Badr, from his father who said, ‘Sallam Abu Ali Al Khurasany narrated to me, from Sallam Bin Saeed Al Makhzoumy who said,

‘While we were seated in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, there came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, Abbad Bin Kaseer of the people of Al-Basra, and Ibn Shurayh, a jurist of the people of Makkah, and in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was Maymoun Al-Qaddah, a slave of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>.

So Abbad Bin Kaseer asked himasws saying, ‘O Abu Abdullahasws! In how many clothes was Rasool-Allahazwj enshrouded?’ Heasws said: ‘In three clothes – two clothes of Suhary and a cloth of Hibra, and there was scarcity regarding Al-Burd’. So it was as if Abbad Bin Kaseer frowned due to that. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The palm tree of Maryamas, rather was of Ajwa (dates), and it descended from the sky. So whatever was from its origin, was Ajwa, and whatever was from its seeding, so it is scrap’.

So when they exited from his<sup>asws</sup> presence, Abbad Bin Kaseer said to Ibn Shureyh, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I don’t know what this example was which Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> struck for me’. So Ibn Shurayh said, ‘This boy will inform you, for he is from them<sup>asws</sup>’, meaning Maymoun. So he asked him, and Maymoun said, ‘Do you not know what he<sup>asws</sup> said to you?’ He said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! No’. He said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> struck an example of himself<sup>asws</sup> for you, so he<sup>asws</sup> informed you that he<sup>asws</sup> is from the children of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and the knowledge of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> is with them<sup>asws</sup>. So whatever comes from them<sup>asws</sup>, so it is correct, and whatever comes from the presence of others, so it is scrap’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people has narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Hassan ibn Yazid from Badr from his father who has said that Salam abu Ali al-Khurasani narrated to me from Salam ibn Sa‘id al-Makhzumi who has said the following.

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) that ‘Abbad ibn Kathir, the devoted worshipper of Basra, and Shurayh, the Faqih, (scholar of law) of the people of Makka came to see The Imam (a.s.). In the presence of abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) already there was Maymun al-Qaddah, the slave of abu Ja‘far (a.s.).

‘Abbad ibn Kathir then asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), “O abu ‘Abdallah, how many pieces of cloths were used to shroud the Holy Prophet (s.a)?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “With three pieces. Two of them were Suhari (made in Suhar, Yemen) and one Hibara (made in Hibara, Yemen). Burd (fabric made in Yemen) was rare to find. ‘Abbad seemed frowning (as if he did not believe in the rarity of the fabric) at this. The Imam (a.s.) said, “The palm tree of (from which) Mary was ‘Ajwa (a kind of palm tree) and it had come from the heavens. Whatever grew from its roots they were also ‘Ajwa and whatever grew from its date-stones it became of lower quality.”

When they left The Imam (a.s.) ‘Abbad ibn Kathir said to ibn Shurayh, “By Allah, I did not understand his simile that abu ‘Abdallah put forward to me.” Ibn Shurayh then said, “ Ask this boy (Maymun al-Qaddah). He will explain it to you because he is from them.” He then ask the boy and he said, “ Is it true that you did not understand what he said to you?”. He ‘Abbad said, “No, by Allah, I did not understand.” The boy, Maymun al-Qaddah, then said, “The refers to his own self. He informed you that he is one of the children of the Messenger of Allah and the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah is with them. Whatever knowledge would come from them is true and correct and whatever comes from other sources are not genuine.”
